questions.statement: The clock says 3:00. What time is it?
questions.context: En la plaza de Bolívar de Bogotá, el reloj de la catedral marca las 3:00 en punto.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Three thirty is 3:30, but the clock shows 3:00 with zero minutes.
Incorrect. Thirteen is the number 13, and clocks in English say three, not thirteen.
Correct. When the minutes are 00 we say the hour and o'clock: three o'clock.
Incorrect. Half past two is 2:30, which is thirty minutes before 3:00.

questions.explanation: Cuando el reloj marca la hora exacta (minutos en 00) decimos el número y "o'clock": "It's three o'clock". "Half past" y "thirty" significan y media, que no es el caso.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Grandma says: "You can turn on the TV now." What can Emilia do?
questions.context: Emilia está en su casa en Sincelejo y su abuela le dice que ya puede prender el televisor.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Doing homework is writing school tasks; turning on the TV is for something else.
Correct. When you turn on the TV, you can watch TV programs.
Incorrect. Taking a shower is washing in the bathroom, not using the TV.
Incorrect. Having dinner is eating the evening meal, which does not need the TV.

questions.explanation: "Turn on the TV" significa prender el televisor. Cuando el televisor está prendido podemos "watch TV", es decir, ver televisión. Las demás opciones son rutinas que no usan el televisor.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: "We do experiments with water and ice in ____ class."
questions.context: En la clase de ciencias de un colegio de Riohacha, los niños hacen experimentos con agua y hielo.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Music class is for singing and instruments, not experiments with ice.
Incorrect. Spanish class is for reading and writing in Spanish, not experiments.
Correct. Science is the class where you do experiments with water, ice and nature.
Incorrect. P.E. is for running and sports, not experiments with water and ice.

questions.explanation: Los experimentos ("experiments") se hacen en la clase de ciencias, que en inglés se llama "Science". "Music", "Spanish" y "P.E." son otras materias con actividades distintas.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: "I ____ basketball with my cousins on Sundays."
questions.context: Los domingos, Miguel juega baloncesto con sus primos en un parque de Medellín.

options.feedback: Correct. With ball games we use play: play basketball, play soccer.
Incorrect. We use go with -ing activities like go swimming, not with basketball.
Incorrect. We use do with activities like do karate or do homework, not with ball games.
Incorrect. Make means to create something, like make a cake; it does not go with sports.

questions.explanation: Con los deportes de pelota como "basketball" y "soccer" usamos el verbo "play". Decimos "go swimming" o "do karate", pero nunca "go basketball" ni "make basketball".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "School starts at seven o'clock. Tomas arrives at half past seven."
Is Tomas early or late?
questions.context: En un colegio de Cali las clases empiezan a las 7:00 de la mañana y Tomas llega más tarde.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Early means before 7:00, but half past seven is after seven o'clock.
Incorrect. On time means at 7:00 exactly, and Tomas arrives thirty minutes after.
Incorrect. Half past seven is 7:30, not seven o'clock.
Correct. Half past seven is 7:30, which is 30 minutes after school starts.

questions.explanation: "Half past seven" significa las siete y media (7:30). Si el colegio empieza a las 7:00, Tomas llega 30 minutos después: llega tarde, en inglés "late". "Early" sería llegar antes.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "My dad gets home at 6 p.m. He has dinner at 7 p.m. He watches TV at 8 p.m."
What does he do at seven?
questions.context: El papá de Nicolás trabaja en Valledupar y sigue la misma rutina cada noche.

options.feedback: Correct. The text says "He has dinner at 7 p.m.", so at seven he eats dinner.
Incorrect. He watches TV at 8 p.m., one hour after seven.
Incorrect. He gets home at 6 p.m., one hour before seven.
Incorrect. The text does not say when he goes to bed; at seven he has dinner.

questions.explanation: Hay que buscar la hora 7 p.m. en el texto: "He has dinner at 7 p.m.". Las 6 son para llegar a casa ("gets home") y las 8 para ver televisión ("watches TV").
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "On Thursday, Natalia has Math at 8:00, Art at 10:00 and P.E. at 12:00. She needs her sneakers to run."
At what time does she need her sneakers?
questions.context: Natalia estudia en Girardot y revisa su horario del jueves para saber cuándo usar los tenis.

options.feedback: Incorrect. At 8:00 she has Math, and in Math she does not run.
Incorrect. At 10:00 she has Art, where she paints and draws, not runs.
Incorrect. No class is at 11:00 in the text, so that time does not match.
Correct. P.E. is at 12:00, and in P.E. she runs, so she needs sneakers then.

questions.explanation: Los tenis ("sneakers") se usan para correr ("run") en educación física, "P.E.". En el horario, "P.E." es a las 12:00 ("twelve o'clock"), así que esa es la hora correcta.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "Sebastian likes sports with a ball and a net. He doesn't like water."
Which sport is best for him?
questions.context: Sebastian vive en Cartagena y busca un deporte nuevo para practicar en el colegio.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Swimming is in the water, and Sebastian doesn't like water.
Correct. Volleyball uses a ball and a net, and it is not in the water.
Incorrect. Running does not use a ball or a net.
Incorrect. Cycling uses a bike, not a ball and a net.

questions.explanation: Sebastian quiere un deporte con pelota ("ball") y red ("net") y no le gusta el agua ("water"). El voleibol, "volleyball", cumple las dos pistas. Nadar usa agua y correr o montar bicicleta no usan red.
questions.subject: ingles
